newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends off lows amid delivery uncertaint.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends off lows amid delivery uncertaint.

text.p: IPE gas oil finished lower on Monday but trimmed losses near the close amid continued uncertainty over the outcome of the record delivery against expiry of the November contract.
Thin volumes allowed prices to move easily and Dec gas oil finished down $2.00 at $218.75, up from a $216.75 low.
Dec lost ground to Jan, cutting its premium by a third to $3 amid concerns the November delivery might slip into December.
Most physical gas traders expect the major recipient of the 865,100 tonne delivery to send some of its oil to Asia.
But much will have to stay in the local ARA market and for transport up the Rhine.
Barge dealers on Monday were already complaining that barges were queueing to take delivery and that deliveries might have to extend beyond the November 30 deadline.
Dealers said energy futures had followed through Friday's minor reversal after sharp gains in the middle of last week but that support looked steady for the time being.
"Things seem to be reasonably steady at these levels so we're not expecting any major sell-off," said one IPE broker.
Jan Brent, nevertheless, flirted with support at $23 and at 1800 GMT was near the day's low, down 31 cents at $22.99 a barrel.
Colder than normal weather in Europe and due to arrive in the United States later this week would help underpin the market, dealers said.
